SEEN 2010.title: Introduction to New Energy Science and Engineering
SEEN 2010.description: This course introduces students to the basics of new energy science and engineering, including: various new energy sources used by mankind; renewable sources; physical foundations for energy consumption and energy production; strategies to optimize renewable energy production and utilization, including wind, solar, bio, and hydrogen energy. Advanced energy storage technologies (such as batteries) and their safety will also be covered. AI-driven material designs for energy applications will be introduced. This course will also discuss the environmental consequences of energy conversion.

SEEN 2030.title: Thermodynamics
SEEN 2030.description: Fundamental concepts; pure substance; work and heat; control volume; Ideal and real gases. First and second laws of thermodynamics. Entropy. Elementary power and refrigeration cycles.

SEEN 2040.title: Fluid Mechanics
SEEN 2040.description: Fundamental concepts; hydrostatics; integral and differential equations of fluid flows; conservation of mass, momentum and energy; dimensional analysis; pipe flow; channel flow and boundary layers.

SEEN 3000.title: Industrial Training
SEEN 3000.description: The industrial training program provides different modules of practical training for energy and environment engineering students to give them a broad and structured understanding of engineering practice and help them satisfy the training requirements of the Hong Kong Institution of Engineers (HKIE) and the UK's Engineering Council for certification/registration purposes. This course will build the bridge between the knowledge acquired in the classroom and engineering practice to enhance student’s understanding and appreciation of the knowledge from the academic courses. By exposing the students to the problem-based exercise, this course will equip the students with hands-on experience in real life equipment, materials, instruments, tools, and automation systems for modern engineering. The students will also have the opportunity of applying modern artificial intelligence technologies in engineering practice, which will help the students succeed in the context of the industry 4.0 transition. Graded P or F.

SEEN 3010.title: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering
SEEN 3010.description: This course delves into the realm of electrical technologies within the context of sustainable energy and the environment. It encompasses a wide range of topics, such as fundamental concepts and principles, essential components and instruments, impedance analysis, the design and analysis of DC and AC circuits, power and efficiency calculations, power converters, and electrical machines. By the conclusion of this course, students will possess not only a profound comprehension of electrical technologies but also robust design capabilities to develop and optimize new electric circuits.

SEEN 3040.title: Heat Transfer
SEEN 3040.description: Transient and steady heat conduction. Natural and forced convection. Radiative exchange. Introduction to computational methods.

SEEN 3060.title: Control Principles
SEEN 3060.description: Introduction to system equations, block diagrams, signal flow graphs, state-space systems, transient response using convolution integral, root locus and frequency response methods. Design by root locus, frequency response and state space method. Nyquist stability test.

SEEN 3070.title: Life Cycle Assessment
SEEN 3070.description: Smart and sustainable solutions are globally on the rise. Product developers, designers, engineers from all sectors use Life Cycle Assessment to use quantitative evidence to proof that their product or innovation is truly more sustainable than existing solutions. Life Cycle Assessment is one of the most commonly used tools to measure the environmental, social and financial cost of a product or system and to allow a fair comparison. In this class students will (1) learn how to assess environmental life cycle impacts and identify options for resource conservation, and pollution prevention; (2) apply methods for Life Cycle Assessment on various products and systems, interpret results and judge the associated uncertainties; (3) interpret and evaluate case examples to gain a deeper understanding of the strengths, weaknesses and appropriate use of Life Cycle Assessment; (4) learn the necessary software basics to perform a moderately complex LCA under supervision.

SEEN 4170.title: Energy Storage Technology
SEEN 4170.description: Electrochemical energy conversion and storage technologies such as fuel cells, batteries, electrolyzers, supercapacitors, solar cells, CO2 reduction, etc. help overcome the energy and environmental problems that have become prevalent in our society. This course will deliver the electrochemistry fundamentals first and then focus on the principles, critical materials, limitations, current status and development trend for each technology.

SEEN 4180.title: Environmental Control
SEEN 4180.description: Wastes from the process industries. Behavior of toxic chemicals in atmospheric, soil and aquatic environments. Adsorption/desorption, air stripping, steam stripping, supercritical extraction. Pyrolysis, biological, catalyzed and uncatalyzed reactions. Integrated environmental control. Instructor's approval is required for non-CBME students' enrollment in the course.

SEEN 4190.title: Environmental Chemistry
SEEN 4190.description: Chemical phenomena in the hydrosphere, lithosphere and atmosphere; their interaction with the biosphere; origin and treatment of pollutants and hazardous waste; environmental monitoring and analysis.

SEEN 4901.title: Final Year Design Project
SEEN 4901.description: SEEN 4901 is a course designed for the students who are in their final year of graduation. The course offers students the opportunity to design and undertake a year-long research project under the supervision of a faculty member in SEE thrust. Students must have their own design task and independent mission in the project. AI-assisted programming should be used in the project. The findings will be presented in the form of a thesis. Credit load will be spread over a year. Instructor’s approval is required for enrollment in the course. This course aims at providing students with a pathway towards designing a project based on a given topic and conducting cross-disciplinary research, allowing the student to explore cooperative project design under the guidance of a faculty member. Grading Type: Letter Grade + PP

SEEN 5010.title: Experiment Design and Analysis
SEEN 5010.description: This course aims to introduce principles in the design of experimental research and practical skills in the statistical analysis of results. Topics will include construction of research hypotheses, principles of statistical inference, confidence interval estimation, and differences in statistical approaches in the trials setting. It will also introduce students to skills and tools for optimal experimental design, experimental data extraction, validation, comparison and uncertainty analysis.
cilos: Understand the significance of experiment design for research in the sustainable energy and environment area
Be familiar with statistics
Be familiar with various parameter estimation methods
Know how to design physical experiments
Know how to design computer experiments
Be familiar with machine learning and surrogate modeling techniques

SEEN 5020.title: Design and Optimization of Energy Systems
SEEN 5020.description: This course aims to introduce techniques for the architecture design, optimization modelling and the economic evaluation of industrial processes and energy systems and to develop the skills required to identify the opportunity and implement optimization-based decision support tools in energy processes and systems. It covers the problem statement, modeling of processes and systems, solving methods for the simulation and the single and multi-objective optimization strategies. Topics cover process systems engineering, process and system modelling and simulation, economic evaluation, optimization strategies, and data reconciliation.
cilos: Recognize structures and dynamic behavior of energy systems
Master mathematical modeling and response analysis methods of energy systems
Learn and apply linear process control theories, including controller structure design, parameter tuning, and stability analyses
Execute real-time optimization and model predictive control methods for multi-objective energy system design
Recognize the energy systems of distributed drive electric vehicles and design optimized control algorithms
Apply the learned control and optimization techniques in dealing with a new scientific problem

SEEN 5030.title: Battery Sustainability
SEEN 5030.description: Rechargeable batteries, as one of the most versatile energy storage technologies, play a central role in the ongoing transition from fossil fuel to renewable energy. This course will focus on the environmental footprint, sustainability, and the diagnostics of batteries. History, fundamental science, and cutting-edge research will be covered in the lectures.

SEEN 5040.title: Modeling and Simulation of Complex Energy Systems
SEEN 5040.description: The subject of transport phenomena includes three closely related topics: fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and mass transfer. Fluid dynamics involves the transport of momentum, heat transfer deals with the transport of energy, and mass transfer is concerned with the transport of mass of various chemical species. In this course, we study these three transport phenomena together. This course will also introduce various solution methods and software tools to tackle the transport phenomena equations in the form of coupled differential equations. Transport phenomena applications in several example systems (e.g., chemical and electrochemical reactors, fuel cells and batteries) will be highlighted.
cilos: Understand the significance of mathematical modeling in process and energy systems engineering.
Be familiar with mathematical modeling and parameter estimation.
Be familiar with thermodynamics and kinetics of fluid systems.
Be familiar with mass, energy, and momentum transfer.
Know how to reformulate and solve coupled differential equations.
Know how to solve transport equations with software tools.
Be familiar with transport modeling for various energy devices and systems.

SEEN 5050.title: Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics: from Molecular to Global Scale
SEEN 5050.description: Chemistry and physics are present everywhere, including the air we breathe. This course provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamental chemical and physical processes that govern the Earth's atmosphere, from the molecular to the global scale. Upon completion of this course, students will understand how a small molecule like ozone can impact the Earth's ecosystem and human health by affecting regional air quality and global climate change. The course content includes an in-depth study of chemical cycles, reaction kinetics, thermodynamics, transport, photochemistry, radiative balance, gas-phase chemistry, and aerosol chemistry. Students will explore the chemistry and physics behind key environmental issues such as air pollution, acid rain, the ozone hole, and climate change.
cilos: Describe major atmospheric environmental issues on earth and human health.
Gain knowledge of the physical and chemical processes in the atmosphere and the mechanisms.
Demonstrate a capability to integrate knowledge and to analyze, evaluate and manage the different aspects of a special topic in Atmospheric Physics and Chemistry.
Apply the learned techniques to real problems related to the chosen topic in Atmospheric Physics and Chemistry.
Develop research topics which are in line with the current developments and trends in the area of Atmospheric Physics and Chemistry.
Assess scientific literature by reading research articles.
Form ideas and present their research clearly through oral presentations.

SEEN 5060.title: Greenhouse Gas, Air Pollutant Emissions and Mitigation
SEEN 5060.description: The aims of this course are to assist students understand emission characteristics of greenhouse gas and air pollutants and their sources, how to characterize and quantify emissions for diverse source sectors, and how to mitigate greenhouse gas and air pollutant emissions. The topics will include: the introduction of greenhouse gases and air pollutants; the characteristics of sector-based greenhouse gas and air pollutant emission sources, sampling and measurement techniques, and commonly used bottom-up estimation methods for major sectors such as energy, industry, transportation, households, and others; the uncertainty and validation of bottom-up emission inventory; the application of big data and innovative methodologies to emission inventory development; and major strategies and green technologies for mitigating greenhouse gas and air pollutant emissions.
cilos: Understand emission source characteristics of greenhouse gases and air pollutants and their environmental impacts.
Understand major methods, instruments and techniques for measuring, calculating and reducing air pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions for major source sectors.
Apply a range of quantitative methods to build air pollutant and greenhouse gas emission inventories.
Understand and apply a range of methods to conduct uncertainty analysis and validation of greenhouse gas and air pollutant emission inventory.
Understand and apply a range of big data-based methods to develop near-real-time greenhouse gas and air pollutant emission inventory.
Apply a range of qualitative and quantitative methods to analyze emission reduction potentials of different techniques or policy scenarios.

SEEN 5090.title: Physical Chemistry of Advanced Energy Materials
SEEN 5090.description: The development of sustainable energy heavily relies on the advancements of corresponding key energy materials. The material’s quality and system stability are closely determined by the related physical chemistry process. This course introduces main concepts and practical application of thermodynamics and kinetics of the key energy materials. It includes basic laws of classical and irreversible thermodynamics, phase equilibria, theory of solutions, chemical reaction thermodynamics and kinetics, surface phenomena, diffusion etc. This course would provide students with insights and deep understandings of the physical chemistry aspects of materials and enable the students to conduct energy material syntheses and energy system experiments with advanced thermodynamic and kinetic foundations.
cilos: Know how to use modern thermodynamic models for the description of a chemical reaction and phase transformation in energy materials.
Gain insights into the energy-related materials and materials processes from both thermodynamics and kinetics point of view.
Understand the laws of thermodynamics and solution theory of materials.
Examine and evaluate microstructural evolution.
Describe the kinetics of the mass transport in solids including the process of surface and interfaces.
Apply the fundamentals of materials thermodynamics and kinetics to energy material engineering and design.
Demonstrate independent and critical thinking, and develop a growth mindset.

SEEN 5100.title: Hydrogen Energy and Fuel Cell
SEEN 5100.description: This course covers hydrogen properties, use and safety, fuel cell technology and its systems, fuel cell engine design and safety, and design and maintenance of a heavy-duty fuel cell engine. The different types of fuel cells and hybrid electric vehicles are presented. The system descriptions and maintenance procedures focus on proton-exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells with respect to heavy-duty transit applications. The PEM fuel cell engine was chosen as it is the most promising for automotive applications, and its transit application is currently the most advanced.
cilos: Develop a basic understanding of the chemical and physical foundations of hydrogen fuel production, hydrogen economy; and the electrochemical, thermodynamic and transport processes governing fuel cell operation.
Calculate fuel cell efficiency; estimate losses and performance; calculate fuel/oxidant consumption rates and water/heat production rates.
Gain a perspective on materials for fuel cells and develop an understanding of their characterization and transport properties.
Develop an understanding of the advantages, limitations and suitability of various fuel cell technologies in transportation, stationary and portable applications.
Acquire technical competency in fuel cell technology including design, performance assessment, and quantitative analysis related to proton-exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells.
Develop an appreciation for practical aspects of fueling and fuel cell system integration and operation.
Enhance awareness with respect to sustainability and the role and impact of energy in society.

SEEN 5110.title: Global Energy and Environment Policy
SEEN 5110.description: This course systematically introduces world energy system and the energy transition, together with theoretical and practical understanding of how energy policies are designed, shaped, advocated and implemented. Trends and projections of global energy will be evaluated, including key technologies, investment trends and subsidy policies. Afterwards, case-based teaching will be given to understand the drivers and constraints associated with national energy policy decision-making. Finally, regional and global energy policies and associated stakeholders will be discussed.
cilos: Understand world energy system and the energy transition, together with theoretical and practical understanding of how energy policies are designed, shaped, advocated and implemented.
Acquire critical knowledge and skills to understand the energy trilemma and the trade-offs that governments have to make in designing energy policies objective.
Identify political economy constraints, key technologies, investment trends and subsidy policies for global energy transformation.
Cultivate capability in critical thinking, systematic thinking, dialectical analysis, and cross-disciplinary investigation for complex problem solving.

SEEN 5120.title: Lifecycle Energy and Economic Analytics
SEEN 5120.description: This course aims to introduce the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of integrated ‘source-grid-load-storage’ multi-energy system frameworks. Environmental impacts will be specifically analyzed, associated with the entire life cycle of a particular product or process. Introduction to Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) will be given for evaluating the economic performance of a specific technology. Three different LCA approaches are introduced, i.e., attributional LCA, consequential LCA, and a hybrid (benchmarking) LCA approach. Physical meaning andcalculation approach of multiple indexes will be holistically introduced, including net direct energy consumption,levelized cost of energy, net present value, discounted payback time, LCA carbon emission, and so on. Afterwards,different application scenarios (like PV, wind turbine, battery, latent heat storages, and integrated PV-battery-building-grid systems) of LCA approach will be given to help students to learn how to apply the approach forlifecycle energy and economic analytics.
cilos: Learn the basic knowledge, understand the principles and mechanism on lifecycle energy/economic analytics in various energy systems, like conversions and storages.
Apply a range of qualitative and quantitative research methods to assess techno-economic feasibility of sustainable energy technologies.
Cultivate capability in critical thinking, systematic thinking, dialectical analysis, and cross-disciplinary investigation for complex problem solving.
Deliver multi-criteria decision-making on various technologies through LCA analytics.

SEEN 5130.title: Green Building in Sustainable Development
SEEN 5130.description: This course is to systematically and comprehensively introduce energy consumption and carbon emission in buildings. Heat transfer mechanism and thermodynamics in HVAC will be introduced. Effective solutions on how to achieve low-carbon buildings will be introduced, such as energy-saving in green building technologies (active and passive strategies), distributed renewable energy systems, energy storages (thermal/ electrical/hydrogen), building energy conversion and management. Techno-economic-environmental analysis will be introduced, together with lifecycle carbon quantification and carbon reduction.

SEEN 5140.title: Digitalization and Intelligence of Integrated Building Energy Systems
SEEN 5140.description: This course aims to introduce the current situation on biologically inspired intelligence in smart buildings. Students will be well trained to conduct statistical analysis and programming experiments; to learn the principles of Artificial Neural Network, fuzzy logic, optimization algorithms and their applications to engineering problems. Technologies for the building role transition from traditional consumers towards prosumers will be comprehensively introduced through ‘source-grid-demand-storage-usage’. Peer-to-peer energy trading, cost-benefit business models and internet of energy things will be introduced. Lastly, in order to guarantee the power supply reliability during extreme weather or war period, energy resilience of distributed energy supply systems will be introduced. Multi-disciplinary areas will be involved in this subject, like fundamentals of artificial intelligence, thermodynamics, heating, ventilation and air conditioning, system modelling and simulation, renewable energy, energy economics, energy policy, and so on.

SEEN 5150.title: Kinetic Energy Harvesting and Conversion
SEEN 5150.description: The course will discuss kinetic energy harvesting devices and systems, including: Principles of energy harvesting from wind, wave, water flow, vibration, and human motion; Architectures and design; Mechanism, electromechanical modeling and analysis of electromagnetic, piezoelectric, triboelectric, electrostatic generators; Lab experiments; Wind turbines and fluid-structure interaction; Fundamentals of vibration; Control and power conditioning circuits; Performance evaluation and optimization; Potential applications and sensing.

SEEN 5160.title: Integration Study of Energy, Transportation, Information and Humanity
SEEN 5160.description: From the view of integration and digitalization, this course aims to paint a picture of what could happen next in industrial development. It will integrate digital technology and power electronics technology to develop energy digitization and promote the energy revolution. Specifically, this course introduces the evolution from industry 1.0 to 5.0, solar power and storage system, data center and AI server power supply, intelligent and electrified transportation, smart charging network and policy, etc.

SEEN 5170.title: Electric Drives and Control Techniques
SEEN 5170.description: Electric drives are power units of electric vehicles, robotics, more electric aircraft, etc. Precise control of electric drives determines the dynamic performance in positioning, speed regulation, and torque generation. This course will give a comprehensive introduction to electric drive structures and control techniques.

SEEN 5180.title: Advanced Thermal Management for Electronics and Power Batteries
SEEN 5180.description: This course introduces concepts in the thermal management of electronics systems and power batteries. Traditional and innovative methods for heat dissipation from electronic systems, and assessment of these methods over a range of applications and scales, will be covered. Novel ultrathin flexible vapor chamber heat spreaders and microchannel heat sinks will be introduced and discussed. Some special emphasis is given to industry applications to discuss thermal management trends.
cilos: Describe, and assess cooling problems in electrics and power battery systems.
Perform thermal design work using air cooling, liquid cooling, phase change techniques.
Describe different liquid cooling techniques and assess their capability and applicability.
Design ultrathin heat spreader, and assess the impact of wick performance.
Assess and optimize the surface modification techniques on cooling performance.
Describe the surface wettability pattens on pool/flow boiling heat transfer systems.
Describe and design microchannels for phase change heat transfer cooling.
Assess the capability and applicability of different thermal management techniques.

SEEN 5190.title: Carbon Capture and Utilization
SEEN 5190.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the technologies and strategies involved in capturing and converting carbon dioxide (CO₂) from industrial processes and the atmosphere. Students will explore the science behind carbon capture methods and emerging technologies for converting CO₂ into valuable products. The course also covers the economic, environmental, and policy considerations driving the development and deployment of carbon capture and conversion systems.
cilos: Know the international and national energy and carbon emission status.
Explain the significance of carbon capture and utilization technologies.
Understand different carbon capture technologies.
Understand different carbon utilization technologies.
Understand the energy policy and principles of carbon tax and carbon trading.
Know how to perform life-cycle environmental assessment on a specific technology.
Know how to design materials and processes for carbon capture and conversion.

SEEN 5200.title: Air Quality Models and Application
SEEN 5200.description: This course provides a comprehensive exploration of commonly used air quality models and their innovative applications in air quality management. It covers numerical air quality models and statistical modeling frameworks, with a focus on key techniques such as emission processing, meteorological modeling, dispersion modeling, photochemical air quality modeling and receptor models. The course highlights recent advancements in AI for air quality modeling and analysis. Through case studies, students can explore real-world applications such as air quality forecasting, pollution source identification, control strategy formulation, and health risk assessment. The course equips students with technical skills to address air pollution challenges and improve policy and public health outcomes.
cilos: Understand basic concepts of air pollution and air quality modeling.
Understand the importance and roles of air quality modeling in air quality management.
Learn how to use air quality models to simulate or forecast air quality, and to analyze the fate and transport of air pollutants.
Learn how to apply air quality models to air pollution study, policy making and exposure assessment.
Understand the progress, challenge and potential of AI-based air quality models.
Demonstrate critical thinking and problem-solving skills in applying air quality models to address air pollution issues.

SEEN 5210.title: Energy Materials and Systems
SEEN 5210.description: Materials are critical for the developments of advanced energy systems, which play a pivotal role towards the sustainable, carbon-neutral future. This course will introduce the working principles of a few energy systems such as fossil fuel, renewable energies, batteries, and supercapacitors. Special focus will be placed on the material aspects of these energy systems through the interrelationships of composition, processing, structure, properties, and performance.
cilos: Identify scientific and engineering significances in energy materials.
Understand the materials physics and chemistry in energy systems.
Apply a range of qualitative and quantitative research methods for conducting the material research for energy applications.
Grasp fundamental research insights and innovative ideas effectively.
Demonstrate independent and critical thinking, and develop new ideas towards better energy materials and systems.
Combine cross-disciplinary tools to address the scientific and technological challenges.

SEEN 5220.title: Environmental Exposure and Risk Assessment
SEEN 5220.description: This course explores the sources, impacts, and control measures for different types of environmental pollutants, covering topics such as air pollutants, drinking water pollutants, and soil pollution (including organic pollutants and heavy metals), etc. Students will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to design and implement effective pollution control measures for diverse environmental challenges.
cilos: Describe key environmental pollution issues and their associated risks.
Apply analytical techniques to monitor and predict environmental pollution scenarios.
Design appropriate control and mitigation strategies for various environmental pollutants.
Differentiate between emission sources and assess corresponding control measures.
Develop and apply analytical reasoning to address interdisciplinary problems in atmospheric and environmental sciences.

SEEN 5230.title: Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics
SEEN 5230.description: This course introduces numerical methods and data structures to analyze and solve problems involving fluid flows. The contents will include Euler and Navier-Stokes equations governing the fluid flow; Mathematical character of partial differential equations; Discretization approaches with a focus on the finite difference method; Explicit and implicit solution techniques and their numerical stability; Verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification; Algorithms for solving the Navier-Stokes and energy equations; Introduction to special topics including finite volume method, turbulence modeling and fluid-structure interaction.
cilos: Identify the role of Computational Fluid Dynamics in solving complex engineering problems related to fluid flows.
Explain the principles governing fluid flows as described by the Euler and Navier–Stokes equations.
Demonstrate proficiency in analyzing the mathematical character of model PDEs relevant to fluid dynamics.
Apply finite difference methods to convert governing equations into solvable algebraic systems.
Implement basic explicit and implicit solution techniques.

SEEN 5240.title: Indoor Air Quality and Healthy Buildings
SEEN 5240.description: Air quality is critical to human health and well-being, as COVID-19 highlighted. This course covers an introduction to contaminants, measurement, exposures, health effects, building systems, human responses, and indoor modeling technologies.
cilos: Describe major indoor air contaminants, their sources and impacts.
Gain knowledge of the physical and chemical processes in indoors.
Analyze, evaluate and manage the different aspects of in indoor air quality.
Apply the learned techniques to real problems in indoor air quality.
Develop research topics which are in line with the current developments and trends in the area of indoor air quality.
Assess scientific literature by reading research articles.
Form ideas and present their research clearly through oral presentations.

SEEN 5250.title: Fundamentals of Transport Phenomena in Energy Systems
SEEN 5250.description: This course will describe the fundamental physical principles that govern the transport of momentum, energy and mass in energy systems. We will start by introducing the constitutive equations of mass transfer, heat conduction and momentum transport in continuum, and solve the conservation equations under given conditions. We will then gain deeper insight into the microscopic physical pictures of these transport phenomena from the perspectives of molecular kinetics, Boltzmann transport equation and wave propagation. From this course, students will acquire a clear physical picture of transport phenomena in energy systems and the ability to analyze them across time and length scales.
cilos: Describe the fundamental physical pictures of momentum, energy, and mass transport at both continuum and molecular scales, and identify the dominant transport mechanisms in a given system.
Apply the constitutive laws (Newton's, Fourier's, Fick's) to formulate fluxes and construct the governing conservation equations for mass, energy, and momentum.
Solve the governing conservation equations by applying appropriate initial and boundary conditions to obtain profiles of velocity, temperature, and concentration.
Evaluate the performance of macroscale energy system components (e.g., heat exchangers, reactors, separators) by applying principles of transport phenomena.
Evaluate the performance of microscale energy conversion devices by linking their efficiency to the underlying transport physics of energy carriers.
Design a conceptual solution for a simple energy transport challenge, justifying design choices using fundamental transport principles and calculated results.

SEEN 5260.title: Energy-efficient Separation Technologies
SEEN 5260.description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of advanced separation technologies, with a particular emphasis on non-thermal methods such as membrane separation. The course will introduce various separation technologies, the fundamental principles and key design considerations essential for effective membrane separation and their unique roles for diverse industrial applications.
cilos: Recognize the current research trends in energy-efficient separation technologies.
Explain the theories and applications of membrane separation technology.
Apply the methodologies and techniques to real problems in the industrial separation processes.
Evaluate the application potential of a given separation membrane.

SEEN 5270.title: Air Quality Measurement Techniques
SEEN 5270.description: Air pollution is a leading environmental risk factor, and it is closely linked with climate change. Effective management of air quality depends on reliable measurements of air pollutants. This course covers atmospheric composition, major and emerging air pollutants and greenhouse gases, and practical techniques for measuring them, including remote sensing, mobile monitoring, and low-cost sensors, illustrated with locally relevant case studies.
cilos: Describe the composition and physical structure of the atmosphere, and the major classes of gaseous and particulate air pollutants.
Explain the operating principles, strengths, and limitations of key gas- and particle-phase air quality measurement techniques.
Apply appropriate sampling, calibration, and QA/QC procedures to generate reliable air quality datasets.
Design field or laboratory measurement strategies to address specific air quality research questions.
Analyze and interpret air quality data using quantitative methods, including uncertainty assessment and comparison across techniques.
Critically evaluate published and real-world air quality measurements in terms of method selection, data quality, and suitability.
Communicate measurement results and insights effectively through written reports and oral presentations, demonstrating independent and critical thinking in air quality research.

SEEN 5310.title: Bio-inspired Energy Systems
SEEN 5310.description: This course aims to introduce energy technologies that are inspired by bio systems and those that can be potentially applied in bio systems. Bio-inspired energy technologies such as biomimetic functional surfaces, bioinspired energy conversion or fuel production, and bionic energy and mass transport and distribution will be covered. Meanwhile, the applications of advanced energy technologies in bio systems such as bio-compatible energy systems, energy supply for artificial skeleton, and self-powered bio sensing will be reviewed.
cilos: Understand the significances and prospects of bioenergy technologies
Grasp the principles of different kinds of bioenergy technologies and resources, their role in renewable energy sources, their constraints, and application preferences
Transfer fundamental research insights and innovative ideas effectively and experience the application oriented design, analysis and evaluation of bioenergy technologies and systems
Demonstrate independent and critical thinking, and develop a growth mindset, an innovative spirit, and a global vision in the field of bioenergy
Apply a range of qualitative and quantitative research methods for conducting cutting-edge research and exploring applications in bioenergy technologies

SEEN 5320.title: Machine Learning in Advanced Energy Systems
SEEN 5320.description: The course aims to introduce main machine learning techniques and their applications in energy systems. The topics will include: 1) the basic concept of machine learning, big data, and energy system; 2) both basic and the state-of-the-art techniques in machine learning; 3) the application of machine learning in energy systems, especially for power systems and smart grids. The goal of the course is to prepare the students for careers in energy and artificial intelligence related areas by teaching data-driven perspective.
cilos: Understand the basic concepts of energy systems, big data, and machine learning.
Be familiar with supervised learning.
Be familiar with unsupervised learning.
Know how to apply machine learning to energy systems.
Know how to use Python for machine learning and energy data analysis.

SEEN 5330.title: Electrical Power Systems
SEEN 5330.description: This course aims to introduce electrical power systems and electrical to mechanical energy conversion, which has become increasingly important as a way of transmitting and transforming energy in industrial, military and transportation uses. It focuses on the power storage, transmission, and conversion as well as control technologies in sustainable energy systems and electric transportation systems including electrical and hybrid electric cars. It covers fundamentals energy handling electric circuits, power electronic circuits such as inverters, and electromechanical apparatus, modeling of power systems, and control and management in power systems.
cilos: Recognize basic laws and structures of electrical power systems
Identify underlying principles of circuits, networks and transmission lines
Apply the basic theories of converters and inverters to explain and predict phenomena related to electrical energy conversion
Describe energy systems of electric vehicles and fundamentals of wireless power transfer
Analyze and solve problems involving EV energy systems and electric motor drives

SEEN 5360.title: Inorganic Photovoltaic Materials and Devices
SEEN 5360.description: Photovoltaics plays a critical role in harvesting solar energy and secures our future sustainable and carbon-neutral society. This course introduces the mainstream photovoltaic technologies specially focused on the ones based on inorganic materials. It covers the fundamental operation and design principles for inorganic photovoltaics, technological challenges, and applications. It also provides the students with the future technological trend and basic knowledge as well as visions in the research and development of inorganic materials based photovoltaic technologies.
cilos: Identify the characteristics of sunlight, and calculate the incident solar power on the surface regarding the orientation and location, etc.
Competently communicate description of silicon solar cell technology and operation
Identify the design aspects of silicon solar cells such as doping concentration profiles, light management, etc.
Identify the characterization methodologies to measure the properties of a solar cell and research frontline for next-generation photovoltaic technologies
Know the classification and operation principles of inorganic compound based solar cells
Identify the design principles and key issues of next-generation tandem solar cell technology
Demonstrate independent and critical thinking, an innovative spirit, and a global vision in the solar energy conversion field

SEEN 6000-6010.title: Special Topics in Sustainable Energy and Environment
SEEN 6000-6010.description: Selected topics of current interest in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.
cilos: Develop interdisciplinary concepts and knowledge in the chosen topics in Sustainable Energy and Environment
Acquire foundational knowledge and theories of the chosen topics
Appreciate the latest research trend and state-of-the-art techniques in the chosen topics
Apply the methodologies and techniques to real problems in the chosen topics
Explain the theories and applications in the chosen topics

SEEN 6100.title: Independent Study
SEEN 6100.description: An independent study on selected topics carried out under the supervision of a faculty member.
cilos: Demonstrate mastery of the knowledge and skills in the selected topics related to Sustainable Energy and Environment.
Apply an interdisciplinary approach in examining the selected topics.
Critically evaluate different aspects of the selected topics.
Communicate findings effectively in written reports.

SEEN 6990.title: MPhil Thesis Research
SEEN 6990.description: Master's thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Identify the current development and the scientific and engineering problems in the field of Sustainable Energy and Environment.
Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Sustainable Energy and Environment.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
Synthesize and create new knowledge, and make a contribution to the field.

SEEN 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
SEEN 7990.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Identify comprehensively the current development and the original scientific or technical problems in the field of Sustainable Energy and Environment.
Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Sustainable Energy and Environment.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
Demonstrate mastery of knowledge in the chosen field of research.
